newsitem.title: USA: Dakota Mining to acquire USMX.
newsitem.headline: Dakota Mining to acquire USMX.

text.p: USMX Inc said Friday it has executed a definitive merger agreement with Dakota Mining Corp.

Under the terms of the merger, USMX said, its shareholders would receive one Dakota common share for every 1.1 common shares of USMX held and USMX would become a wholly owned subsidiary of Dakota. USMX now has 16.2 million common shares outstanding while Dakota has 35.5 million shares outstanding.
USMX said the merger is subject to approval by the Toronto Stock Exchange, shareholder and creditor approval, review by other regulatory authorities and other customary conditions.

The merger sets the stage for the combined company to become a mid-sized gold producer with production of some 140,000 ounces annually commencing in 1997, growing to 200,000 ounces in 1998, USMX said in a statement.

The combined company should have excellent opportunities to expand the reserves on existing properties and a highly prospective portfolio of exploration properties in North and Latin America and would expect to pursue additional acquisition opportunities.

Alan R. Bell, president and chief executive officer of Dakota, would be the president and chief executive officer of the merged company; and Donald P. Bellum, chairman, president and chief executive officer of USMX, would be the chairman of the board, the statement said.
The board would consist of four USMX appointees, including one designated by USMX's largest stockholder, Pegasus Gold Inc, and five Dakota appointees.
